http://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/27920.text: Big News Network.com Romanian jet shoots down drone The UAV was tracked from the Black Sea and destroyed over an "unpopulated area," according to the Romanian Defense Ministry A Romanian F-16 fighter jet has shot down a drone that entered the country's airspace, President Nicusor Dan has said. The drone incursion has not yet been blamed on any foreign military. In a post on X, Dan said that the drone was intercepted around 11 am on Friday, and that an investigation has been launched. The Romanian Defense Ministry said that the drone was picked up by radar over the Black Sea earlier on Friday morning, and was tracked as it moved westward towards the port of Sulina. It was intercepted over an "unpopulated area" around Padina, 90 km northeast of Bucharest, and destroyed with an air-to-air missile, the ministry added. The incident is the third of its kind in Romania over the last two months. On June 5, a Ukrainian naval drone exploded near an oil terminal in Constanta, Romania's largest Black Sea port, while three more detonated offshore. The drones were operated by the Ukrainian navy, which claimed that it lost control of the devices. On May 29, a UAV carrying explosives crashed into an apartment building in Galati, 20km from the Ukrainian border. Authorities in Bucharest identified the drone as a Russian 'Geran-2' kamikaze drone, claiming that it could have been hit by Ukrainian air defenses and veered off course. Dan's response was dramatically different in the two cases. The Romanian president made no formal complaint when the Ukrainian naval drone entered the country's main port while others exploded off Constanta, describing the incident as an unfortunate consequence of the "military operation led by Ukraine against Russian aggression." After the drone crash in Galati, Dan ordered the closure of the Russian consulate in Constanta and attempted to trigger NATO's Article 4, which is invoked when a member state determines that their "territorial integrity...or security" is threatened. Dan also announced that he would "accelerate Romania-Ukraine cooperation on the co-production of drones" and increase military aid to Kiev. Russia argued that its Geran drones carry higher payloads of explosives than the UAV that struck the apartment building, and that a stricken Geran would not have been able to cover the distance from Ukrainian air defense positions to Galati. Moscow suggested that the incident was used by Bucharest to justify plans made in advance - such as closing the consulate and stepping up aid to Kiev. https://us.cnn.com/2026/08/15/europe/dro.text: Russia says it shot down more than 800 Ukrainian drones overnight in what appears to be among Ukraine’s largest aerial attacks on Russia, with authorities reporting at least six people killed. The two sides have escalated their air war on one another, with Ukraine increasingly firing barrages of drones at targets deep inside Russia, including warehouses and industrial plants as well as refineries. Russia’s state-run TASS News said it was the largest Ukrainian drone attack since the beginning of the year – with many of the drones targeting the Moscow area where many of Russia’s elite reside. Air defense forces and electronic warfare units shot down and neutralized 187 drones over the Moscow region, according to its governor, Andrey Vorobiev. Geolocated video showed a huge fire at a Wildberries warehouse in the Moscow region, the Russian equivalent of Amazon. Vorobiev said no one was injured. Wildberries’ warehouses have been repeatedly targeted by Ukrainian drones in recent months. Ukraine says it has struck seven out of Wildberries’ ten largest logistics centers. The warehouse struck on Sunday was 250,000 square meters, the Ukrainian military said. Kyiv has claimed that Wildberries handles supplies for the Russian military, and has stepped up its targeting of other critical parts of the Russian economy. The company recently announced that it would build new warehousing in neighboring Kazakhstan. One person, an 83-year-old man, was killed by a drone attack elsewhere in Moscow region on Sunday, according to Vorobiev. Drones were intercepted over 17 regions – mainly in southern and western Russia – according to the Russian Defense ministry. Five people were killed in the Rostov region in southern Russia, according to the governor of that region. A “defense-industrial complex enterprise that produces solid rocket propellant” for various Russian weapons was struck in the attack in Rostov, according to the Ukrainian military. On Sunday, maritime risk management agency Marisks said a Greek oil tanker had been attacked while positioned at a buoy mooring near Russia’s port of Novorossiysk. The company said the vessel was hit twice and Ukraine was likely responsible. But the weapon used, extent of the damage, condition of the crew and status of the cargo remain unconfirmed. No let up in Russian fire Russia meanwhile continues to target the Ukrainian capital Kyiv with a mix of missiles and drones. Six people were wounded by strikes early Sunday, according to Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky. A book market in Kyiv was among the sites hit. Kremenchuk and Kryvyi Rih in central Ukraine were also struck by ballistic missiles, Zelensky said. Two people were killed in Kryvyi Rih and another in Sumy in the north, Zelensky said. Thirteen employees of a steel factory in Kryvyi Rih were injured and one person died, according to Arcelor Mittal, which operates the plant. Rescue and search operations are ongoing, it said. Ukraine did not shoot down any of the ballistic missiles fired at it overnight, according to an Air Force statement, again highlighting its short supply of missiles interceptors. Russia fired more than 1,550 attack drones, nearly 1,560 guided aerial bombs and 62 missiles at Ukraine over the last week, according to Zelensky. “European interceptors cannot simply be allowed to sit in storage. Lives need to be protected. Russia must be stopped,” he added. Elsewhere, an unidentified drone was shot down Sunday in Romanian airspace, according to the Defense ministry in Bucharest. The drone was intercepted by a Spanish F-18 fighter jet pilot on a NATO air policing mission. It was the fourth drone shot down this year over Romania, the defense ministry said. The ministry said its radars detected the drone entering the country from neighboring Moldova. Fragments appeared to have fallen in an uninhabited area between two villages. In July, Romanian F-16 fighter jet pilots shot down three Russian drones breaching national airspace for the first time after dozens of such incursions in the more than four years of Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine. This story has been updated.

https://hotnews.ro/tara-care-blocheaza-v.text: Ministerul Afacerilor Externe din Finlanda a anunţat joi că guvernul va interzice de acum înainte accesul sportivilor ruşi pe teritoriul său, ca urmare a războiului din Ucraina purtat de Rusia. „Atâta timp cât războiul de agresiune al Rusiei continuă, sportivii ruşi nu au ce căuta în Finlanda”, a declarat Elina Valtonen, ministrul de externe de la Helsinki. „Intrarea lor în ţară ar reprezenta o ameninţare la adresa relaţiilor internaţionale ale Finlandei. Acelaşi lucru este valabil şi pentru alte activităţi profesionale pe termen scurt, efectuate în baza unor vize, care nu sunt esenţiale pentru interesele naţionale ale Finlandei”, a adăugat oficialul, conform News.ro. Ministerul de Externe al Finlandei a declarat că această măsură îi va afecta atât pe sportivii ruşi care concurează sub statut neutru, cât şi pe cei care concurează în cadrul echipelor naţionale. Finlanda va găzdui săptămâna viitoare un Grand Prix de patinaj artistic şi, tot în această lună, o etapă a Cupei Mondiale de schi fond. Ambele sporturi permit sportivilor ruşi să concureze ca „sportivi neutri”. Un eveniment important care va fi afectat este Campionatul Mondial de patinaj artistic din luna martie. Se preconizează că patinatorii ruşi se vor număra printre principalii pretendenţi la medalii. Federaţia Internaţională de Patinaj (ISU) a declarat că „a luat act de declaraţia făcută de guvernul finlandez cu privire la intrarea cetăţenilor ruşi în ţară şi la posibilele consecinţe asupra evenimentelor sportive, inclusiv asupra campionatului mondial de patinaj artistic al ISU, care urmează să se desfăşoare la Tampere, în Finlanda, şi analizează implicaţiile acesteia”. „ISU consideră că sportivii nu ar trebui să fie pedepsiţi pentru acţiunile guvernelor lor într-o lume în care, din păcate, sunt în curs numeroase conflicte”. ISU a adăugat că „solicită clarificări” din partea oficialilor din domeniul patinajului din Finlanda. Modificarea intră în vigoare începând de luni, aşa că nu ar trebui să afecteze meciurile din NHL de săptămâna aceasta de la Helsinki dintre Seattle Kraken şi Carolina Hurricanes, nici cursele de slalom din Cupa Mondială de schi programate la Levi sâmbătă şi duminică. Finlanda se numără printre echipele europene care s-au angajat să nu joace împotriva Rusiei la Campionatele Mondiale de hochei pe gheaţă. Campionatele masculine sunt programate să se desfăşoare în Germania, care analizează în prezent dacă va continua să organizeze evenimentul. Pe termen lung, Finlanda urmează să găzduiască Campionatele Europene de atletism în 2030. World Athletics, forul de conducere al acestui sport, menţine o interdicţie generală privind participarea Rusiei, deşi aceasta face obiectul unei acţiuni în justiţie. https://www.novinite.com/articles/241482.text: iNews Novinite Econ DoctorOnline Jenite Div Sporta FitWell Sportuvai Peika Programata News in English BUSINESS POLITICS WORLD SOCIETY SPORTS Latest Culture Crime · Hotels 5* · Hotels 4* · Hotels 3* · Apartment Houses · Bar&Restaurants · Rent-a-car · Casino · Sport · Mountain resorts · Sea resorts · Education · Entertainment · Shopping · Health Clinics · Beauty Zone · Public Safety · Business Finance Best in BG Novinite Insider · Radisson Blu · 4 Seasons · French Survey · Investors Survey · Austrian Survey · Italian Survey · US Survey · Greek Survey · Dutch Survey Special Topics EU Southeast Europe Russia Ukraine International Business Von der Leyen to Meet Radev in Bulgaria Over Black Sea Attacks Tweet Share Send to Kindle European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will visit Bulgaria next week for talks with Prime Minister Rumen Radev in Varna and a visit to the Nikola Vaptsarov Naval Academy, as attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea raise security concerns along NATO's eastern flank, a Commission spokesperson announced. Von der Leyen is scheduled to arrive in Varna on Tuesday, November 10, as part of a tour of the Black Sea region prompted by strikes against commercial vessels off the Bulgarian and Romanian coasts. The details were presented during a European Commission briefing on her schedule for the coming week, BTA reported. Her regional mission will begin on Monday, November 9, with meetings in Bucharest with Romanian President Nicușor Dan and Prime Minister Luca Niculescu. On Wednesday, she is due to attend a United Nations-organized climate change conference in Turkey. The Commission president had previously announced plans to visit Bulgaria during her policy address to the European Parliament at the beginning of the new political season, when she presented the European Commission's priorities for the year ahead. At the time, she proposed holding a "Regional Connectivity Summit" with the Bulgarian prime minister in the spring, focusing on the "Middle Corridor" initiative linking Europe to Asia. However, the escalation of hostilities in the Black Sea has brought forward her visit to Bulgaria. The planned trip follows a series of drone attacks against commercial vessels, which have heightened tensions near NATO territory. Several sailors have been killed and dozens remain missing. On November 6, a drone was also discovered washed ashore near Shabla on Bulgaria 's Black Sea coast. Three European Commission officials familiar with the arrangements confirmed the visit to Politico. One of the officials, who spoke anonymously because of the sensitivity of the security situation, described the shipping route as "Currently, this is the deadliest maritime route in the world." At least seven commercial vessels have been hit by drones in the Black Sea over the past month. The attacks have killed two sailors, while at least 25 people are still missing. Romania has accused Russia of carrying out strikes that have brought the war in Ukraine dangerously close to NATO territory. Bucharest has described the attacks as part of Moscow's increasingly aggressive campaign against Ukraine. Bulgaria has not officially attributed the attacks to Russia, saying only that the drones came "from an easterly direction." Concerns grew further on November 6 after a local resident found a drone that had washed up near Shabla. Mayor Mariyan Zhechev said the unmanned aircraft had most likely been brought to the coast by sea currents. Its origin remains unknown, and it has not been established whether it is connected to the recent attacks on commercial vessels. It is also not yet clear whether von der Leyen will be accompanied on her visit by other senior European officials, including European Council President António Costa or EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs Kaja Kallas. The attacks have prompted calls for a coordinated response. In mid-October, after drones struck the first two vessels near Bulgaria 's coast, von der Leyen condemned the incidents and expressed the European Union's support for Bulgaria and Romania. Radev subsequently called on the Commission president and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte to work together to stop attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea. Bulgaria has also requested a moratorium on hostilities across the Black Sea basin, where tensions have intensified as the war between Russia and Ukraine has expanded. Five commercial vessels have been struck within Bulgaria 's exclusive economic zone, some of them sinking. Bulgaria intends to seek 2 billion euros in compensation for attacks on commercial vessels in its exclusive economic zone. Nine countries could receive additional EU financial assistance during the next programming period to compensate for losses resulting from the war in Ukraine. A delegation of Members of the European Parliament recently visited Varna, delivering the message that Europe was united and Bulgaria was not alone. The EU's position is that Black Sea security extends beyond the region itself, affecting European security and the stability of its common future. NATO allies have increased surveillance over the Black Sea following the attacks on commercial shipping. On Tuesday, Italian, British and U.S. reconnaissance aircraft were detected conducting missions over the region simultaneously. France has also extended the deployment of a maritime patrol aircraft in Romania. Diplomatic efforts to protect commercial shipping have intensified as well. At a G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta on Saturday, November 7, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said India and Turkey had submitted proposals aimed at ensuring safe passage for grain-carrying vessels through the Black Sea while the war between Russia and Ukraine continues.
